rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent carved bar/court mass in all four views, not just one view, so it clears the visual coherence gate. The dominant gesture is understandable: a compact rectilinear volume with a substantial U-shaped or slot-like void and a split/raised condition toward the center. The green parcel is respected broadly; the mass sits within it and the long axis tracks the site rather than ignoring it. The blue frontage edge is answered only moderately well: the building does produce a void/entry seam, but the access response is somewhat indirect and the ground edge still feels more sealed than explicitly public. Program-wise, it plausibly supports neighborhood living because the mass is low-rise, hierarchical, and has a usable court/terrace logic, but the section is not yet as expressive or generous as the best references. The main weakness is that the upper mass reads a bit generic and boxy, with the void doing most of the work; still, the overall composition is repairable and not over-collided.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact mass can still feel public when a large carved court and bridge-like connector organize the building around a clear threshold.
Terraced low-rise blocks around a central plaza show how distributed volumes can preserve a strong collective void.
An elongated low-rise body with a courtyard void and slight roof articulation can support mixed-use without becoming tower-like.
The strongest transferable move is a campus-like arrangement with connected wings and an occupied terrace/court sequence.
Interlocking volumes with a central void and lifted connections can keep the ground active while allowing upper mass variety.

warnings: Frontage response is present but could be more legible as a public threshold aligned to the access edge.
Section remains somewhat generic; a stronger roof/section articulation would better support the neighborhood-living brief.
Void is credible, but its publicness is moderate rather than emphatic.
